records.name: Lipetsk Oblast
records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no region-specific trans-related evidence for it: hostility here is legislated federally and administered by federal security services, so the division inherits the national picture (score 0.12; deviation vs national ±0.02). The federal layer applying here: the 2023 ban on legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care; the propaganda law (up to 15 days' detention plus deportation for foreign visitors who 'promote' non-traditional relationships); the 'LGBT extremism' designation regime (101 convictions, 146 fines in 2024); and uncorrectable document markers, so any police, hotel or transport identity check reads a mismatch.

sources.claim: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity for Russia (June 2025) is the national framework this division is assessed against: consensual same-sex activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned; the Supreme Court designated the international LGBT+ movement an 'extremist' organisation in November 2023; between 2022 and 2024 at least 139 individuals were affected by anti-LGBT+ law enforcement, with 'gay propaganda' fines for individuals up to 400,000 rubles (about £3,600) or 15 days' detention, and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023. The note contains no information specific to this division beyond that national framework.

Human Rights Watch (30 June 2025): Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for participation in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its symbols since the Supreme Court's November 2023 designation, with defendants facing up to 12 years in prison; HRW also documented 81 people found guilty in 98 cases since January 2024 of administrative offences (article 20.3) for displaying banned LGBT symbols, mostly on social media. This national enforcement baseline underpins the national score this division is assessed at; the article contains no division-specific detail.

records.name: Ulyanovsk Oblast
records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score.

sources.claim: UK Home Office country policy and information note on Russia, SOGI (June 2025): same-sex sexual activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned, gender-marker changes on documents are prohibited, and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023; the 2013 'gay propaganda' law is punishable by administrative fines (up to 400,000 rubles for individuals) or detention of up to 15 days, with repeated offences escalating to criminal prosecution and up to four years' imprisonment, and since the November 2023 Supreme Court 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement, participation carries 2-6 years and organising 6-10 years' imprisonment (Article 282.2). Records at least 139 people in Russia impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws between 2022 and 2024 and assesses that openly LGBT+ people are likely to face discriminatory treatment that, by its nature or repetition, may amount to persecution, the state able but not willing to provide protection. Region-specific: citing an October 2024 OVD-Info report, the note records that Ilya Zhuravlev, former head of the dialysis centre in Inza in the Ulyanovsk region, was detained in August on charges of participating in the activities of the 'extremist' 'LGBT movement' (Part 2 of Article 282.2) and coercion of a person to act of a sexual nature (Part 1 of Article 133) - the regional enforcement of the federal framework this record claims.

Human Rights Watch (30 Jun 2025): Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions (about 98 administrative, 3 criminal) for alleged participation in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its symbols since the 2023 Supreme Court 'extremist' designation; between January 2024 and June 2025 at least 20 people faced criminal charges, including three publishing-house staff charged in May 2025 under Article 282.2 who each face up to 12 years' imprisonment, and 81 people were found guilty in 98 administrative cases under Article 20.3 for displaying banned symbols. Region-specific: in March, a Ulyanovsk-region doctor who faced a maximum of one year's imprisonment for alleged sexual coercion was also prosecuted for 'involving' another man in the 'LGBT movement' and received a three-year sentence - the federal enforcement wave in operation inside this region, whose national score the record adopts.
